entity.name: Thomas Jefferson
entity.description: The man who wrote "all men are created equal" while owning 600 slaves. Third U.S. president, principal author of the Declaration of Independence, founder of the University of Virginia, and architect of the Louisiana Purchase that doubled America's size. Died on July 4, 1826 — the 50th anniversary of the Declaration.

story.name: Thomas Jefferson
story.description: Drafts the Declaration of Independence, doubles America's territory with the Louisiana Purchase, founds a university, and dies on the 50th anniversary of the nation he helped create. The contradictions of liberty's architect.

moments.name: Thomas Jefferson Is Born at Shadwell Plantation in Colonial Virginia
moments.subtitle: The third of ten children inherits 5,000 acres and a world of contradictions
moments.description: On April 13, 1743, Thomas Jefferson was born at his family's Shadwell Plantation in the Colony of Virginia. His father, Peter Jefferson, was a planter and surveyor; his mother, Jane Randolph, came from one of Virginia's most prominent families. Jefferson was the third of ten children. He inherited approximately 5,000 acres upon his father's death in 1757, including the land where he would later build Monticello. A fire destroyed Shadwell in 1770, consuming Jefferson's first library of 200 volumes — a loss that devastated the obsessive book collector.

moments.name: Jefferson Drafts the Declaration of Independence in a Rented Room
moments.subtitle: A 33-year-old writes the most consequential sentence in American history
moments.description: In June 1776, the Second Continental Congress appointed a five-member committee to draft a declaration justifying American independence from Britain. The committee delegated the writing to 33-year-old Thomas Jefferson, who composed the document over 17 days in a rented second-floor parlor at the home of bricklayer Jacob Graff in Philadelphia. Jefferson's opening assertion that "all men are created equal" drew on Enlightenment philosophy, particularly John Locke's theories of natural rights. Congress adopted the Declaration on July 4, 1776. The document became the foundational statement of American democracy.

moments.name: Jefferson Buys 828,000 Square Miles from France for $15 Million
moments.subtitle: The president who championed limited government makes its boldest expansion
moments.description: In 1803, President Thomas Jefferson negotiated the Louisiana Purchase, acquiring approximately 828,000 square miles of territory from Napoleon's France for $15 million — roughly four cents per acre. The deal, signed on April 30, 1803, doubled the geographic size of the United States overnight, extending its western boundary from the Mississippi River to the Rocky Mountains. Jefferson had originally sent envoys only to buy New Orleans and its port. Napoleon, needing funds for European wars, offered the entire territory. The purchase challenged Jefferson's own strict-constructionist reading of the Constitution, which nowhere authorized such an acquisition.

moments.name: Jefferson Founds the University of Virginia and Designs Its Campus
moments.subtitle: The only U.S. president to found a major university, he called it his proudest achievement
moments.description: In 1819, Thomas Jefferson founded the University of Virginia in Charlottesville, personally designing its campus in the neoclassical style. Jefferson envisioned an "academical village" centered on a grand Rotunda modeled after the Roman Pantheon, flanked by colonnaded pavilions housing professors and students. The university opened on March 7, 1825, with 68 students. It was the first American university to separate education from religious doctrine. Jefferson considered its founding — not his presidency — among his greatest achievements, listing it on his self-authored epitaph alongside the Declaration of Independence and the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom.

moments.name: Jefferson Dies on July 4, 1826 — Exactly 50 Years After the Declaration
moments.subtitle: His last rival John Adams dies the same day, whispering "Jefferson survives"
moments.description: On July 4, 1826, Thomas Jefferson died at Monticello at age 83, exactly 50 years to the day after the Continental Congress adopted his Declaration of Independence. In a coincidence that stunned the nation, his longtime friend and rival John Adams died the same day in Quincy, Massachusetts. Adams's reported last words were "Thomas Jefferson survives" — not knowing Jefferson had died hours earlier. Jefferson was buried at Monticello beneath an obelisk he designed himself, inscribed with three achievements he chose: author of the Declaration, the Virginia Statute for Religious Freedom, and father of the University of Virginia. The presidency was not listed.
